# -gcflags patterns that match on a package's directory or on whether it is in
# the standard library must also apply to packages that only the test loads:
# the test's own imports and the generated test main's dependencies.

[!compiler:gc] skip 'using -gcflags'

# std= overrides all= for test-only standard-library packages.
go test -a -c -n -gcflags=all=-e -gcflags=std= ./z
stderr 'compile.* -p example.com/z .* -e '
stderr 'compile.* -p example.com/z/helper .* -e '
stderr 'compile.* -p testing .*'
! stderr 'compile.* -p fmt .* -e '
! stderr 'compile.* -p testing .* -e '

# std= applies to test-only standard-library packages.
go test -a -c -n -gcflags=std=-e ./z
stderr 'compile.* -p testing .* -e '
! stderr 'compile.* -p example.com/z/helper .* -e '

# A relative pattern applies to packages only the test imports.
go test -a -c -n -gcflags=./...=-e ./z
stderr 'compile.* -p example.com/z/helper .* -e '
! stderr 'compile.* -p testing .* -e '

# The same holds for the test of a package with only _test.go files.
go test -a -c -n -gcflags=all=-e -gcflags=std= ./onlytest
stderr 'compile.* -p example.com/z/helper .* -e '
! stderr 'compile.* -p runtime .* -e '
! stderr 'compile.* -p testing .* -e '

# The work pattern depends on the module that p.load sets.
go test -a -c -n -gcflags=work=-e ./z
stderr 'compile.* -p example.com/z/helper .* -e '
! stderr 'compile.* -p testing .* -e '

# go vet compiles the same packages.
go vet -a -n -gcflags=all=-e -gcflags=std= ./z
stderr 'compile.* -p testing '
! stderr 'compile.* -p testing .* -e '

# sync/atomic is loaded by EnsureImport when building with atomic coverage,
# and nothing else in this library imports it.
go build -a -n -cover -covermode=atomic -gcflags=all=-e -gcflags=std= ./lib
stderr 'compile.* -p sync/atomic '
! stderr 'compile.* -p sync/atomic .* -e '
stderr 'compile.* -p example.com/lib .* -e '

go build -a -n -cover -covermode=atomic -gcflags=std=-e ./lib
stderr 'compile.* -p sync/atomic .* -e '
! stderr 'compile.* -p example.com/lib .* -e '

-- go.mod --
module example.com

go 1.25
-- z/z.go --
package z

import "fmt"

func Hello() { fmt.Println("hello") }
-- z/z_test.go --
package z

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/z/helper"
)

func TestHello(t *testing.T) { helper.Check(t) }
-- z/helper/helper.go --
package helper

import "testing"

func Check(t *testing.T) { t.Log("checked") }
-- lib/lib.go --
package lib

func F() int { return 1 }
-- onlytest/x_test.go --
package onlytest

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/z/helper"
)

func TestX(t *testing.T) { helper.Check(t) }
